name: Collagen
aliases: collagen, hydrolysed collagen, hydrolyzed collagen, collagen hydrolysate, collagen peptides, bovine collagen, beef collagen, porcine collagen, pork collagen, fish collagen, marine collagen, chicken collagen, poultry collagen
what_is: An animal protein ingredient derived from connective tissues such as hides, skins, tendons and, for specified species, bones. Food collagen can be declared generically or with an animal source.
why_botia: BOTIA flags collagen because it is of animal origin and a source-specific declaration can matter for dietary choice. EU hygiene rules list permitted animal raw materials for food collagen. A generic word such as collagen does not identify the source species or establish halal status.
can_1: Detect collagen, collagen peptides, hydrolysed/hydrolyzed collagen and explicit bovine, porcine, fish or poultry source terms.
can_2: Show the animal-origin and Muslim-choice context, using the source only when it is actually declared.
cannot_1: Identify the animal species when the label says only collagen.
cannot_2: Certify halal status, slaughter method, processing route or cross-contact from the generic ingredient name.

sources.label: Regulation (EC) No 853/2004 — Section XV, collagen intended for food
